minutes.headline: Parks Commission rescinded and re-voted the skatepark location to the Marshall Park master plan site and elected new officers.
minutes.summary: The commission approved April and May minutes, then voted to move the skatepark's approved location to the Weston & Sampson master-plan site (design work only), after a long debate about moving the Marshall Park playground. It also committed to the Board of Health septic offer, recommended demolishing the McNally snack shack, and discussed Marshall Park phasing, the select board meeting date, beach opening, mowing contract and graffiti. Anna Lockwood was elected chair, Dave Pacios vice chair, and Karen clerk.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to rescind its November 2021 skatepark approval and move the skatepark to the Marshall Park master-plan site, for design work only.
The commission voted to commit to the Board of Health's offered septic system with a two-toilet facility at the master-plan location.
It voted to recommend to the town manager that the McNally snack shack be demolished rather than repaired.
The commission agreed to ask the town manager for funding for schematic design of the whole Marshall Park project, with phases 1, 3 and 4 as likely starting points.
Anna Lockwood was elected chair, Dave Pacios vice chair, and Karen was appointed clerk.

why_it_matters: The skatepark's new location and the septic and toilet commitment shape how Marshall Park is phased and what the town may be asked to fund through capital requests and town meeting.
The McNally demolition recommendation and the unresolved mowing contract question touch how the town pays for field and building upkeep, and whether the contract's terms are being met.
watch_next: A joint meeting with the select board is targeted for August 2, with the chair to confirm the time.
The next Parks Commission meeting is set for July 20; the signed landscape contract with its cost breakdown was requested from the DPW director.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all eight non-procedural votes and on the main decisions. They differ on who receives the lifeguard recommendation, on whether the McNally demolition costs more or less than $5,000, and on who does two of the follow-up tasks. The one to check first is the Hennessey vote: ours says the select board, the official minutes say the Town Manager.
